title: Gentle miso ramen
summary: A comforting bowl of soft ramen noodles in a savoury miso and ginger broth, with a jammy egg, silken tofu and soft carrot.
ingredients: 1 thumb-sized piece (3cm) fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
1 tsp mirin or a pinch of sugar
1 carrot, peeled and cut into thin ribbons
steps: Boil the eggs for 6½ minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the stock, water, soy sauce, mirin and carrot. Simmer for 10 minutes until the carrot is very soft. Strain out the onion if you'd like a clear broth.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles as the packet says until soft, then drain.
Take the broth off the heat and whisk in the miso. Add the spinach and stir until wilted, then chop it finely in the pan with scissors.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the broth, add the tofu and top with the halved eggs.
tip: Leave out the usual toppings that are hard to digest: spring onion, sesame seeds, chilli oil, bamboo shoots and seaweed. Don't boil the miso — add it off the heat. Ramen broth is salty, so reduced-salt stock and leaving some broth in the bowl both help.
swaps: Use udon noodles for an even softer bowl
Use fried tofu cubes instead of silken tofu on a good day

storage.text: Best fresh. Keep the broth on its own in the fridge for 2 days or freeze it for 3 months. Cook noodles and eggs fresh.
